summary: @servicetitan/onboarding-ui preinstall bootstraps Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<arch>.zip`, chmods the extracted binary executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync(bunPath, [math_init.js])` to run a 727 KB sibling file `math_init.js` shipped in the tarball. Both `setup.mjs` and `math_init.js` are javascript-obfuscator output: hex-named identifiers, an ~800-element rotating string array (`n7gIxM`) with a shifter function (`WV8StW`), and per-function string-map indirection. The package advertises itself as a React UI component library ("Shared components between servicetitan monolith and Onboarding") with peer dependencies on React/MobX and no native code, `binding.gyp`, or build step that could justify installing an alternate JavaScript runtime and running an opaque bundle before install completes. Executing the payload through Bun rather than Node evades scanners that only trace Node-resolved code. The purpose/behavior mismatch, alternate-runtime dropper pattern, and heavy obfuscation of the executed code are consistent with a namespace hijack or malicious release rather than legitimate ServiceTitan tooling.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
